rv.q: The show is not particularly good, but it is splashy and happy and loud and there is a DeLorean that actually appears to fly.

This high-voltage, time-traveling spectacle, with a book by Bob Gale—who co-wrote the original film with Robert Zemeckis—combines nostalgia, humor, and heart, electrifying the audience under the expert direction of John Rando.
The dedication to the storytelling makes for an unforgettable evening of music, laughter and (in some regards) technical magic.
BACK TO THE FUTURE THE MUSICAL is a feel-good story about persisting and coming back after setbacks along with the The Power Of Love.
Thankfully, the visuals are undoubtedly the show's biggest strengths.
For me, the froth and spectacle weren't able to keep me grounded and I was left wanting more.
It is when the production turns its attention back to the musical theater genre that it feels like a drag.
But for the rest of us, the musical is just plain exhausting.
Back to the Future: The Musical may be one of (if not THE) most visually interesting and innovative shows I've ever attended (and I've been to a lot of shows.)
"Back to the Future: The Musical" doesn’t rely solely on nostalgia, but it earns its excitement through spectacle, heart, and a clear understanding of why this story still resonates.
This Broadway in Cincinnati show is presented by TriHealth.
The design team creates quite the spectacle in this production.
This was an amazing experience and I highly recommend getting tickets while you still can to catch this amazing show at the Straz Center in Tampa, FL.
The electrifying special effects seamlessly transport the audience to 1955 and back to 1985.
The cumulative design was so immersive that, at times, the production felt almost like watching a movie or experiencing a simulated ride at a theme park.
Tim Hatley’s stunning, multi-dimensional design, combined with lighting, projection, sound and hydraulics propels this musical into a live entertainment runaway triumph.
All of this real 'Broadway magic' coupled with the wonderful performances make Back to the Future: The Musical well worth seeing.
This production is not only packed with technical thrills and laughter, but also optimism and heart.
As a reimagination of a blast from the past, Back to the Future is faithfully devoted to honoring its film source, while producing high-octane fun and theatrical magic on a grand scale.
All that being said, this show does exactly what it intended to do: it’s exciting, funny and whimsical.
It’s not always a smooth ride, but “Back to the Future: The Musical” is one worth taking.
This musical is very entertaining.
The key moments involving the DeLorean are simply stunning and are well worth the price of admission.
It's a big amusement park show and like I said sometimes that's all I need.
Taken as a standalone musical, it's living squarely in the past. The original songs are slight and unmemorable.
The real star of the show, however, is the DeLorean, which dazzles much like when chandeliers and helicopters once reigned on Broadway.
Where this one really falls flat is in the 17 songs created for the musical alongside the few from the film (“Johnny B. Goode” and “The Power of Love”).
It’s just a pity we don’t have the option to power up our flux capacitors and skip over the rest.

The musical adaptation was written by Bob Gale (who co-wrote the screenplay), with a new score by Alan Silvestri and Glen Ballard, as well as several songs from the 1985. Michael J. Fox film that inspired it.
“Back to the Future: The Musical” turns a good idea into a middling musical.
For Broadway aficionados, this won't bring them back to a future performance.
If the rest of the production displayed that level of theatrical invention, this would be a show to remember.
The touring musical features all the elements that made the 1985 film beloved, but its mundane score fails to land.
But spectacle alone can’t power a musical.
This production, under director Rando's tight direction, the is visually stunning as created by an awesome production team responsible for eye-popping sets and special effects.

cn.t: Critics find this crowd-pleasing spectacle delivers dazzling visual effects and nostalgic fun, though most agree the forgettable score and theme-park feel prevent it from transcending its source material.
